quotes.text: Muscle is built in the gym, but it is fed in the kitchen.
Training asks your body to spend. Eating is how you refill the account.
Protein at every meal is a simple habit that quietly looks after your strength.
Rest, water and a proper meal make a good workout worth it.
You do not need a perfect workout. You need a walk, a meal and a night’s sleep, again and again.
Strength is a lifelong asset. Feed it while it is easy and it will carry you when it is hard.
Recovery is part of training, and food is part of recovery.
Skip the miracle. A walk, enough protein and a good night’s sleep are less exciting and work far better.
Movement makes you hungry, and food gives you something to move with. It is a beautiful loop.
The best exercise plan is the one your body has enough fuel to finish.
Being strong is not about looking a certain way. It is about carrying your own shopping at eighty.
Eat enough to train, and train enough to enjoy the eating.
Your muscles are made of what you eat. Give them good material.
A walk after dinner is one of the smallest, cheapest and most underrated habits there is.
There is no such thing as too small a workout, only ones that did not happen.
Endurance starts with breakfast.
Fatigue is often less about fitness and more about what and when you last ate.
Do not train on an empty tank and then wonder why it feels heavy.
Stairs count. Walking counts. Carrying things counts. Gardening counts. Just move.
The stronger you get, the more your body deserves real food.
A strong body is a kind of freedom: carrying, climbing, running for the bus, playing with your kids.
You do not have to be an athlete to eat like someone who values their body.
Treat your training and your eating as one plan, not two.
Whatever the workout, a proper meal afterwards is part of the session.
Consistency beats intensity, on the plate and on the mat.
The body adapts to what you ask of it and to what you give it. Ask well and give well.
A daily walk is the most underrated piece of health equipment there is.
Be a little stronger than last month. It is the only comparison worth making.
Energy in, energy out, and the wisdom to leave room for rest.
Move because you can, and eat because it helps you keep moving.
A glass of water before the workout and a proper meal after it. Most of the plan is that simple.
Your body can do more than you think when it has been fed well and rested properly.
The day you feel like skipping is the day a ten-minute walk works best.
Do the workout you can do today, not the one you did in your best month.
Healthy legs, a healthy heart and a healthy appetite tend to arrive together.
Stretch, sip some water, eat something real. The order matters less than doing all three.
Strength grows slowly, then quietly, then suddenly you are carrying two bags up the stairs.
Nobody regrets a walk. Very few regret a good meal after one.
A tired body needs food and sleep before it needs a pep talk.
Every bit of movement is a vote for the body you want to have at seventy.
